pending_articles.title: Low-cost fine-tuning of SmolVLA with smoothness regularization and chunk-aware auxiliary supervision for language-conditioned manipulation
pending_articles.content: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models offer a unified interface for language-conditioned manipulation. This paper reports a negative result: a low-cost post-training recipe for SmolVLA with LoRA, a temporal smoothness regularizer, and chunk-aware auxiliary supervision from action-variation pseudo labels does not improve manipulation success under a 30,000-step budget (approximately 1/67 of the original 2,000,000-step SmolVLA recipe). Because the auxiliary classifier is used only during training and the runtime chunk length remains fixed at k = 8, we denote the configuration SmolVLA+LoRA+S&C (smoothness and chunk-aware auxiliary losses) rather than “adaptive.” We evaluate four LIBERO suites with a unified protocol of 500 episodes per cell (50 episodes × 10 task variants). Over three training seeds, the matched fixed-chunk k = 8 baseline reaches a four-suite macro success rate of 10.9%±1.1, whereas SmolVLA+LoRA+S&C reaches 3.5%±1.4; the pre-specified primary comparison shows significant deficits on LIBERO-Spatial (−16.4 percentage points, exact sign-flip permutation p = 0.004) and LIBERO-Object (−17.5 pp, p = 0.002), with matched-pairs rank-biserial effect sizes of −0.96 and −1.0. Matched component ablations isolate the smoothness loss as the harmful term (smoothness-only collapses performance; chunk-classifier-only approximately matches the baseline), and executed-action logs show the regularizer triples trajectory jerk (1.69 vs. 0.59 RMS)—the opposite of its intent. A training-free inference-time temporal-ensembling baseline, by contrast, more than doubles success on the two suites where the baseline is competent (Spatial 36.2 vs. 19.0%; Object 56.2 vs. 24.0%) at a 2.3 × step-rate cost, and a 10–100K budget sweep shows the S&C deficit never closes. We conclude that, for the tested configuration, budgets, and benchmark, the added action-side losses are not competitive with a well-tuned fixed chunk, and inference-time ensembling is the stronger use of the same compute.

pending_articles.title: Psychomusicology: A resounding closing cadence.
pending_articles.content: From 2012 to 2023, the American Psychological Association served as publisher of Psychomusicology: Music, Mind, and Brain. Annabel Cohen and Mark Schmuckler were the successive editors-in-chiefs during this time. As the journal is ceasing publication, the two editors reflect on the development and progress of the journal in the context of the history of psychology and publication trends. They present their review in 10 short movements each with a unique musical emotional expressivity: overture, amabile, vivace, elegy doloroso, sforzando, capriccio, con brio, pendolo, agilmente, and finale risonante, ending on a very upbeat note! Early on, Psychomusicology offered a much-needed research forum for the psychology of music. More recently, the recognized importance of music psychology to almost all areas of psychology has led to increasing numbers of outlets for publication. During the 12 recent years under APA’s stewardship, the journal more than doubled the number of articles published since the journal’s inception in 1981. The entire corpus of almost 600 articles represents foundational and well-cited contributions to such current research areas as musical expectancy, performance excellence, musical development, neuroscience, emotion, preference, and film music, among others. Cohen and Schmuckler express deep gratitude to the authors, past editorial board members, and reviewers for their contributions to this corpus, and to the American Psychological Association Publications office and staff both for support and, importantly, for holding and making accessible in perpetuity the outstanding scholarship within the archives of Psychomusicology: Music Mind & Brain and Psychomusicology: A Journal of Music Cognition. pending_articles.title: Suggestibility and psychedelics: From therapeutics to social context.
pending_articles.content: Suggestibility is an important aspect of the psychedelic experience that merits greater attention in the expanding field of psychedelic research. This article provides a comprehensive road map for exploring the critical questions and issues at the intersection of suggestion, suggestibility, and psychedelics. Suggestibility is linked to the psychedelic experience, and likewise, psychedelics are associated with enhanced suggestibility, possibly due to their apparent ability to amplify openness and associative thinking. This relationship is one that research has not adequately addressed. Key factors related to the psychedelic experience, including expectation, symbolic thinking, and mindset, are additionally important to examine for both users and researchers. This article examines how psychedelic substances contribute to our understanding of suggestibility and therapeutic techniques, ranging from fostering creativity and alleviating depression to provoking distrust and conspiratorial thinking. By discussing the role of suggestion and suggestibility in psychedelic research, we highlight their applications in clinical, social, and cultural contexts. Recasting historical interpretations of psychedelics through these constructive narratives can significantly benefit various social domains. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved)

pending_articles.title: Evaluating dispositional emotion-related factors in the effect of acceptance on affect reactivity: A secondary analysis of an experimental study.
pending_articles.content: Acceptance as a self-regulation strategy has beneficial effects on affect reactivity in response to stressors via reducing negative affect and state anxiety as well as improving positive affect. However, dispositional emotion-related factors, namely, experiential avoidance, emotional dysregulation, and trait anxiety, may moderate these effects such that higher levels of these factors may weaken or enhance the association between acceptance and affect reactivity. We conducted a secondary analysis of a laboratory-based controlled comparison study that evaluated experiential avoidance, emotional dysregulation, and trait anxiety as potential factors that may moderate the effect of acceptance on state measures of affect and anxiety. One hundred undergraduate students were randomized to an acceptance condition (n = 75) or a no-instruction comparison condition (n = 25). Participants completed self-report measures (a) at baseline, (b) immediately following a fear-inducing film clip, and (c) after a recovery period following the fear-inducing film clip. Multilevel regression models revealed that participants with greater experiential avoidance, greater emotional dysregulation, and lower trait anxiety reported higher levels of positive affect over time. These moderation effects were not observed in the no-instruction comparison condition, which rules out regression to the mean. Findings imply that, when faced with a stressor, acceptance may counteract experiential avoidance and emotional dysregulation to enhance positive affect, whereas trait anxiety may interfere with the ability of acceptance to improve positive affect. Thus, acceptance as a self-regulation strategy targeting positive affect may be well suited for those with higher experiential avoidance, higher emotional dysregulation, and/or lower trait anxiety. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved)

pending_articles.title: Open monitoring meditation defined as the nonreactive meta-awareness of mind wandering.
pending_articles.content: Open monitoring meditation is generally defined as the nonreactive, meta-aware observation of moment-by-moment phenomenal experiences associated with mental contents without focusing on predetermined mental or physical objects. However, in the current literature, neither general definitions nor more technical ones specify any particular mental state as the content of the meditator’s meta-awareness. In this article, we argue at both cognitive and neural levels that the object of the meditator’s meta-awareness consists solely of the phenomenal experiences associated with mind wandering contents, characterized as unguided, spontaneous thoughts. We demonstrate that out of the various definitions of mind wandering, only the one outlined in the dynamic framework aligns with our proposition, which defines open monitoring as the nonreactive meta-awareness of mind wandering. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved)

recently_processed.title: From pose estimation accuracy to motor biomarker reliability: a reliability-centred evaluation framework for markerless movement analysis
recently_processed.content: Markerless pose estimation has become an essential tool for quantitative movement analysis in neuroscience. However, current evaluation frameworks primarily rely on frame-wise spatial accuracy metrics, which provide only limited information about the reliability of the downstream kinematic biomarkers derived from reconstructed trajectories. In this study, we propose a reliability-centred evaluation framework designed to assess the preservation of downstream kinematic information in pose estimation pipelines. The framework was evaluated exclusively using DeepLabCut-based architectures trained and tested under identical experimental conditions. Forelimb trajectories of mice performing the Montoya staircase task were analysed using nine DeepLabCut-based convolutional neural network architectures. We introduce the Motor Biomarker Reliability Composite Score (MBRCS), which integrates four complementary dimensions of trajectory reliability: spatial accuracy, temporal stability, occlusion robustness, and kinematic fidelity. Each component was normalized to a 0–1 scale, where higher values indicate greater trajectory reliability. Although several architectures achieved comparable frame-wise localisation performance, larger differences were observed in temporal stability, occlusion robustness and downstream kinematic fidelity. Across the evaluated architectures, MBRCS values spanned almost the entire normalized range (0.00–0.99). These differences were reflected in the Normalized Jerk Score (NJS), which was used as the downstream kinematic biomarker in this study. Overall, our findings suggest that frame-wise localisation accuracy alone may not fully capture differences in trajectory reliability that become apparent when temporal stability, occlusion robustness and kinematic fidelity are jointly considered. The proposed framework provides a structured and reproducible methodology for benchmarking pose estimation pipelines according to the reliability of downstream motor biomarkers.

recently_processed.title: Dogmatic Bayesianism Disorder
recently_processed.content:
Note: This humorously intended sarcastic blog post directly mimics classifications of psychological disorders in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of the American Psychological Association, but Dogmatic Bayesianism is not in the DSM-5 as an actual psychological disorder - for now.

 

Dogmatic Bayesianism Disorder

Diagnostic Criteria                                              F61.1

A. Individuals are convinced that they know what other people want to know.

 

B. Individuals believe that everyone who is not a Bayesian is wrong. They almost continuously try to convince others, and there is often a strong feeling others need to be ‘saved’.

 

C. Strong tendency to ridicule non-Bayesians, including historical figures. Karl Popper (who opposed Bayesianism, as it opens the door to dogmatism in science) is an especially common target.

 

D. A pervasive obsession with Bayesian statistics, and the use of p-values or hypothesis testing by others, at the expense of flexibility, openness, and acknowledging that other coherent statistical approaches exist to deal with uncertainty.

 

E. Symptoms cause clinically significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of current functioning. The forceful insertion of Bayesian statistics into conversations can drive away conversation partners, to the point where almost all social contact is restricted to other dogmatic Bayesians.

 

F. Individuals believe everyone else will become a Bayesian. Older dogmatic Bayesian often lose bets that everyone will have become a Bayesian by a specific year. If this bet is lost, they continue to claim everyone will become a Bayesian in the future and consider this a rationally updated belief.

 

Specify if:

Persistent: The disorder has been present for more than 12 months.

Specify current severity:

Dogmatic Bayesianism Disorder is specified as severe when an academic exhibits all symptoms of the disorder, at which point individuals are classified as having Bayesian Evangelical Syndrome (BES).

 

Prevalence

Less than 0.01% of the general population is affected, but prevalence is estimated to be at 1% to 2% in statistically inclined academics. Due to diagnostic criterion E prevalence can be up to 80% on certain internet forums. Men are more frequently affected than women, at a ratio estimated at 100:1 or greater.  

Development and course

Development of the condition often starts in the early thirties, but onset can occur at an older age, in which case the symptoms are often much more severe. There is currently no treatment, and dogmatic Bayesianism typically increases with age. In rare cases (less than 1%) spontaneous recovery seems to occur, after which individuals often experience prolonged feelings of shame and embarrassment.

Risk and Prognostic Factors

The disorder is more common in individuals with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD).

recently_processed.title: New Papers: Optimal Filter Settings for ERP Research
recently_processed.content:
Zhang, G., Garrett, D. R., & Luck, S. J. (in press). Optimal filters for ERP research I: A general approach for selecting filter settings. Psychophysiology. https://doi.org/10.1111/psyp.14531 [preprint]

Zhang, G., Garrett, D. R., & Luck, S. J. (in press). Optimal filters for ERP research II: Recommended settings for seven common ERP components. Psychophysiology. https://doi.org/10.1111/psyp.14530 [preprint]

What filter settings should you apply to your ERP data? If your filters are too weak to attenuate the noise in your data, your effects may not be statistically significant. If your filters are too strong, they may create artifactual peaks that lead you to draw bogus conclusions.

For years, I have been recommending a bandpass of 0.1–30 Hz for most cognitive and affective research in neurotypical young adults. In this kind of research, I have found that filtering from 0.1–30 Hz usually does a good job of minimizing noise while creating minimal waveform distortion.

However, this recommendation was based on a combination of informal observations from many experimental paradigms and a careful examination of a couple paradigms, so it was a bit hand-wavy. In addition, the optimal filter settings will depend on the waveshape of the ERP effects and the nature of the noise in a given study, so I couldn’t make any specific recommendations about other experimental paradigms and participant populations. Moreover, different filter settings may be optimal for different scoring methods (e.g., mean amplitude vs. peak amplitude vs. peak latency).

Guanghui Zhang, David Garrett, and I spent the last year focusing on this issue. First we developed a general method that can be used to determine the optimal filter settings for a given dataset and scoring method (see this paper). Then we applied this method to the ERP CORE data to determine the optimal filter settings for the N170, MMN, P3b, N400, N2pc, LRP, and ERN components in neurotypical young adults (see this paper and the table above).

If you are doing research with these components (or similar components) in neurotypical young adults, you can simply use the filter settings that we identified. If you are using a very different paradigm or testing a very different subject population, you can apply our method to your own data to find the optimal settings. We added some new tools to ERPLAB Toolbox to make this easier.

One thing that we discovered was that our old recommendation of 0.1–30 Hz does a good job of avoiding filter artifacts but is overly conservative for some components. For example, we can raise the low end to 0.5 Hz when measuring N2pc and MMN amplitudes, which gets rid of more noise without producing problematic waveform distortions. And we can go all the way up to 0.9 Hz for the N170 component. However, later/slower components like P3b and N400 require lower cutoffs (no higher than 0.2 Hz).

You might be wondering how we defined the “optimal” filter settings. At one level, the answer is simple: The optimal filter is the one that maximizes the signal-to-noise ratio without producing too much waveform distortion. The complexities arise in quantifying the signal-to-noise ratio, quantifying the waveform distortion, and deciding how much waveform distortion is “too much”. We believe we have found reasonably straightforward and practical solutions to these problems, which you can read about in the published papers.

  • Added Global Crisis Support Resources as an Index to Misc > Assistance section.

Stars Added ⭐

  • Starred F-Droid in FOSS APKs, one of the most loved and trusted sources for open source apps. Note that Droid-ify (f-droid frontend) is starred in same section, which is why F-Droid itself hadn't been until now.

  • Starred Limusic in Audio Streaming Apps, seems to be the cleanest, fastest, and most feature-rich / 2 open-source desktop client for YouTube Music currently.

  • Starred lostnode in Video Downloaders, supports 600+ sources, has a nice UI + fast downloads.

  • Starred Kryoto in Game Download, big library, fast host(s), unique UI, has become well liked in a short time.

  • Starred Antra Web in Audio Ripping, works well, supports many formats and websites.

  • Starred VoiceMeeter in System Audio, Well-made virtual audio mixer with Voicemeeter Banana + universal routing for hardware inputs and outputs, aswell as software.

  • Starred Better Lyrics in YouTube Music Tools, has nice themes, accurate sync, and was well liked by users in the suggestion thread.

  • Starred wBlock in iOS Adblocking, fast and feature-rich Safari adblocker with custom blocklist support, userscript/userstyle engine and more.

  • Starred LibraryThing Awards in Book Recommendations, nice index of book awards & winning books, aggregating major prizes, annual lists and more / 2.

  • Starred Retro Online in Retro Browser Emulators, has over 800 games, got a fair amount of positive attention from those who tried it.

  • Starred Autocompressor in Video Tools, has free tier with 2 GB file size limit, fast uploads + downloads, and minimal timeouts.

  • Starred Spoti.pw as it seems to be the best current option for ad-free spotify on iOS.

  • Starred Vicinae in Linux Apps, open-source app launcher w/ easy setup, raycast/script compatibility and more.

  • Starred Mocha in File Hosts, 15GB per file, 100GB storage, keeps files 30 days after last download. ⁠

  • Starred DropDrive in File Hosts, 100GB per file, keeps files 30 days after last download.⁠

  • Starred /mental health/ in Mental Health section, well researched and put together, a fair amount of people have come forward saying they found it helpful.

  • Starred Vorssaint in macOS System Tools, open-source menu bar toolkit with many features / utilities, including a volume mixer, keyboard shortcuts, screen recording, and more.

  • Starred Pawn Appétit in Chess Learning, updated and feature-rich / 2 fork of En Crossiant which we previously had starred.

  • Starred OpeningTree in Chess Learning, pulls a player's match history from Chess.com or Lichess and maps games onto an interactive board / 2.

  • Starred PyChess in Chess Section, takes Lichess architecture and expands it / 2 into a massive, free, open-source museum and battleground for over 60 regional, historical, and fairy chess variants.

  • Starred Accela in Linux Gaming, Steam Game + DLC unlocker, nice ui, good dev team, seems to work well for people.⁠

  • Starred ynoTV in IPTV Players, nice UI, feature rich, score/match finder, custom playlists, trakt/simkl integration and more.

Things Removed

  • Removed GOG Games as it's now officially offline. Huge thank you and respect to their team for maintaining such a uniquely high-quality site for so long.

  • Removed UnTrap (Distraction-Free YouTube Extension) as they seem to of put many useful features behind a paywall.

  • Removed all file hosts that have malicious ads. Note that some of these are planning to switch to different ads on Nov 1st, and may be reconsidered at that time if they follow through.

  • Removed UnionCrax as they're stepping down.
